```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)

table_dir <- file.path("..", "outputs", "tables")
figure_dir <- file.path("..", "outputs", "figures")
```

## Appendix Purpose

This workbook collects the technical evidence that can support the main report
without overcrowding it. The final appendix should be edited into the student's
own presentation style after the final models are selected.

## Data Preparation Details

```{r}
#| label: data-preparation
clean_series <- read_csv(file.path(table_dir, "clean_birth_fertility_series.csv"),
                         show_col_types = FALSE)
series_summary <- read_csv(file.path(table_dir, "series_summary.csv"),
                           show_col_types = FALSE)
validation_checks <- read_csv(file.path(table_dir, "data_validation_checks.csv"),
                              show_col_types = FALSE)

kable(head(clean_series, 10), caption = "First ten analysis-ready rows")
kable(tail(clean_series, 10), caption = "Last ten analysis-ready rows")
kable(series_summary, caption = "Series summary")
kable(validation_checks, caption = "Validation checks")
```

**Student-owned notes to add:**

- State the raw file name and any relevant source note.
- Explain the final selected columns and units.
- State whether validation checks found any issue requiring correction.

## Transformation and Differencing Details

```{r}
#| label: transformation-details
transformation_series <- read_csv(file.path(table_dir, "transformation_series.csv"),
                                  show_col_types = FALSE)
transformation_screen <- read_csv(file.path(table_dir, "transformation_screen.csv"),
                                  show_col_types = FALSE)
recommendation_inputs <- read_csv(file.path(table_dir, "transformation_recommendation_inputs.csv"),
                                  show_col_types = FALSE)
differenced_series <- read_csv(file.path(table_dir, "differenced_series.csv"),
                               show_col_types = FALSE)
stationarity_screen <- read_csv(file.path(table_dir, "stationarity_screen.csv"),
                                show_col_types = FALSE)

kable(transformation_screen, caption = "Transformation screen")
kable(recommendation_inputs, caption = "Transformation recommendation inputs")
kable(head(differenced_series, 12), caption = "Differenced series preview")
kable(stationarity_screen, caption = "Stationarity screen")
```

![Level ACF](`r file.path(figure_dir, "level_acf.png")`)

![First-difference ACF](`r file.path(figure_dir, "first_difference_acf.png")`)

## Candidate Model Specification

The exact fitted model objects are produced in `scripts/03_model_comparison.R`.
The final appendix can use this table to describe the comparison set without
rewriting every formula in the main report.

```{r}
#| label: model-specification
candidate_registry <- read_csv(file.path(table_dir, "candidate_model_registry.csv"),
                               show_col_types = FALSE)
candidate_terms <- read_csv(file.path(table_dir, "candidate_model_terms.csv"),
                            show_col_types = FALSE)

kable(candidate_registry, caption = "Candidate model registry")
kable(candidate_terms, caption = "Candidate model terms")
```

**Equation notes to complete manually:**

- Benchmark models: write the naive or drift form used as a baseline.
- Trend models: write the deterministic trend relationship and error term.
- ARIMA models: state the differencing order and the autoregressive or moving
  average terms selected by the workflow.
- ETS models: state the error, trend, and seasonal components reported in the
  fitted terms table.

## Fit Statistics and Diagnostics

```{r}
#| label: fit-diagnostics
fit_statistics <- read_csv(file.path(table_dir, "candidate_model_fit_statistics.csv"),
                           show_col_types = FALSE)
ljung_box <- read_csv(file.path(table_dir, "residual_ljung_box_tests.csv"),
                      show_col_types = FALSE)

kable(fit_statistics, caption = "Candidate model fit statistics")
kable(ljung_box, caption = "Residual Ljung-Box tests")
```

![Residual time plots](`r file.path(figure_dir, "candidate_model_residuals.png")`)

![Residual ACF plots](`r file.path(figure_dir, "candidate_residual_acf.png")`)

## Holdout Forecast Evaluation

```{r}
#| label: holdout-evaluation
forecast_design <- read_csv(file.path(table_dir, "forecast_design.csv"),
                            show_col_types = FALSE)
holdout_accuracy <- read_csv(file.path(table_dir, "holdout_forecast_accuracy.csv"),
                             show_col_types = FALSE)
best_holdout <- read_csv(file.path(table_dir, "best_holdout_models.csv"),
                         show_col_types = FALSE)
selection_evidence <- read_csv(file.path(table_dir, "model_selection_evidence.csv"),
                               show_col_types = FALSE)

kable(forecast_design, caption = "Holdout design")
kable(holdout_accuracy, caption = "Holdout accuracy")
kable(best_holdout, caption = "Best holdout models by accuracy")
kable(selection_evidence, caption = "Combined selection evidence")
```

![Holdout forecast comparison](`r file.path(figure_dir, "holdout_forecast_comparison.png")`)

## Models Not Selected

Use this section after final model selection. A concise appendix explanation is
enough: identify candidates rejected because of weaker holdout accuracy,
residual dependence, over-complexity for the sample size, or weaker alignment
with the exploratory patterns.
